patients.label: 33-year-old woman brought to the emergency department after lemborexant and eszopiclone overdose with reported alcohol

identity_evidence.quote: A 33-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department (ED) with impaired consciousness

attribution_limitations: CNS depression severity is called mild in the abstract and conclusion but moderate in the discussion for the same GCS 11 presentation.
Intent of the overdose is only implied by her call to her mother; the empty blister packs only suggested an overdose.
Author attributes the initial sedation partly to the co-ingestants eszopiclone and alcohol, but states this as likely or as an interpretation.

The uncaptioned graphical abstract prints "Full Clinical Recovery (GCS 15)" at 9 hours post ingestion, which the text does not state (the text says only that she could ambulate by nine hours and later recovered fully); its plotted GCS line reaches 15 only at the 12-hour tick, so the graphic is internally inconsistent.

limitations: Graphical abstract has no caption or in-text callout; it is described in the visual submission only and its printed values are not added as text facts.
The graphical abstract prints a Glasgow Coma Scale of 15 at nine hours, which the text does not state; chart values estimated from the plotted line or bar are not facts and do not override the text.
Severity of the central nervous system depression is described as mild in the abstract and conclusion and as moderate in the discussion; both are kept as review-only source-conflict facts.
Intent of the overdose is only implied; blister-pack tablet counts are recorded as review-only and not summed into a dose.
Plasma lemborexant was measured at only two time points; the author calls the later level a peak while noting that only two levels were obtained.
Discussion statements about pharmacokinetics, co-ingestant effects and the fatal comparison case are interpretation or other cases and are not patient facts.
